fact: The Star column reports Kenyans filed annual returns and VAT returns on the KRA iTax portal in June and August 2026, with intermittent delays and errors but filing continuing, and VAT filing moved onto iTax from an offline template.

A KRA public notice of 2026-08-31 states suppliers to government entities submit invoices for payment processing through IFMIS, and that eTIMS was integrated with IFMIS by KRA and the National Treasury.

The National Treasury's IFMIS website describes IFMIS as an automated platform covering planning, budgeting, procurement, expenditure management and reporting for national and county governments; no event date is given, so the page's published date 2026-08-30 is used.
A KRA notice of 2026-04-23 states that from May 2026 validated export data from Customs iCMS prefills zero-rated supplies in the VAT return in iTax, which taxpayers already file.

The Kenya Revenue Authority's iTax portal offers online tax services (PIN, compliance certificate and withholding certificate checkers, status checker, forms) under a 2011-2026 copyright; the page gives only a year, so 2026 is its published date.

The Kenya Revenue Authority's November/December 2025 release notes describe enhancements and defect fixes to the live iTax system (VAT registration, returns, refund vouchers, PIN API for foreign investors); these are enhancements, not a new system.

An opinion piece by a named policy analyst calls IFMIS a nationally governed platform to which county revenue systems are meant to connect, and reports the Auditor-General's 2025 finding that Trans Nzoia's system was not yet connected to it.

The Addis Tax Initiative profile lists Kenya Revenue Authority reforms of 2019 that added a risk profiling and monitoring module to the iTax system and integrated iTax with the registration bureau, vehicle registry and business registration service; the profile's own date is 2025 and the stated events are 2019.

The CEG Kenya brief (2018) states the National Treasury rolled out IFMIS for use by national and county governments, covering planning, budgeting, procurement, expenditure management and reporting, without a revenue management module for counties.
